title: xAI to Implement Invisible Text Watermarking for Grok API to Comply With EU Law

tickers.name: Space Exploration Technologies Corp. Class A Common Stock

summary:
The developer of the Grok AI assistant will introduce a system for identifying machine-generated text within its API responses starting Nov. 7. These invisible identifiers will be enabled by default for all regional and global endpoints to ensure the company meets the transparency requirements of the EU AI Act, though team administrators can opt out of the feature for individual models through the management console.

While other leading laboratories including Google and Meta have already adopted similar marking standards to track synthetic media, xAI had remained a notable outlier in the industry. The new implementation closes most of that gap, leaving the North American version of ChatGPT as one of the few remaining major AI models that does not default to text watermarking. It is not yet clear if these identifiers will be applied to Grok's direct chat interface.

selectedTweets.text:
Many of my readers had questions about the upcoming text watermarking for Grok. Here's the official explanation from @spacexai's documentation!

Supported Grok models will include an invisible watermark in their text output, allowing SpaceXSI to identify AI-generated text later. According to SpaceXSI, this is being implemented to comply with the EU AI Act.

Importantly, watermarking is enabled globally, not just in the EU! It applies to all SpaceXSI API endpoints, including the global endpoint and all regional endpoints.

The good news: Watermarking can be disabled! Team admins can opt out for individual models through the SpaceXSI Console.
